messages:
Maria (billing): FYI — CS just escalated. Acme's AP rejected our invoice PDF. They attached it and said their parser failed. Reported problems: bank wire instructions split across pages, VAT ID not labeled (it sits inline with the address), line item descriptions collapsed (parser expects itemized fields), and PO number isn't in a distinct metadata field. They refused to pay. Can we triage?
Noah (support): Uploaded the PDF: https://files.redwood/acme-invoice-2026-03-15.pdf :grimacing: Customer claims their AP parser looks specifically for 'Bank:' or 'IBAN' as a contiguous block and 'VAT ID:' label.
Sergio (engineering): Which template do we use for PDF gen on that account (hosted vs legacy)? If it's the HTML -> wkhtmltopdf flow I can try CSS tweaks: make the bank block non-breakable (page-break-inside: avoid) and add a dedicated PO metadata area.
Maria (billing): This account is on hosted billing, template version v2 (we rolled to most accounts last month). I attached the invoice id: INV-2026-0315-ACME.
Ethan (payments): Repro steps I ran: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.com/billing/invoices/INV-2026-0315-ACME/pdf -> saved file -> same wrap. Root cause appears to be an unbounded beneficiary name that forces the bank line to wrap mid-IBAN.
Olivia (legal): Acme also flagged legal-entity formatting. They require the company registration number and VAT on the same header block labeled 'Legal entity / Tax'. Right now our address block puts VAT after street address without the label — their parser ignores it. We should standardize to 'VAT ID:' or 'Tax ID:' for EU templates.
Sergio (engineering): Quick patch idea (CSS + template):
```
.bank-block { page-break-inside: avoid; white-space: nowrap; }
.bank-block .beneficiary { max-width: 450px; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; }
.metadata .po { display: inline-block; font-weight:600; }
```
If we ellipsify beneficiary we won't split IBAN, but need to ensure full beneficiary visible to human readers — maybe add a tooltip / full text in a separate line.
Ethan (payments): Ellipsify is risky for compliance. For wire instructions we need both readable beneficiary and exact IBAN. Alternative: force bank block to the next page if it doesn't fit (avoid breaking the line). That matches customer requirement.
Maria (billing): Customer also asked if we can provide a machine-readable invoice (JSON/UBL). They said their AP supports e-invoice ingestion. Could be a stopgap.
Noah (support): I'll ask CS to offer the JSON invoice export as a temporary workaround.
Olivia (legal): Also confirm which legal entity string we print for EU invoices. Some customers require full registered name + registration number in same line. I'll audit mapping for the EU legal entity config.
Sergio (engineering): Action items: 1) Patch template to use page-break-inside: avoid for .bank-block and keep IBAN atomic (Sergio) — ETA 48h for patch + CI. 2) Add explicit 'VAT ID:' label in EU header mapping (Sergio + Olivia) — small change. 3) Add PO number to top-right machine metadata block (Ethan/Sergio) — ETA 72h. 4) Offer JSON e-invoice export as workaround (Noah / Ethan) — customer-facing in 24h.
Maria (billing): I'll update Acme: offer JSON and ask if they can accept regenerated PDF after patch.
Ethan (payments): Note: make sure pdf generator doesn't apply word-break: break-all on IBANs. Also add a unit test that renders a long beneficiary + IBAN and asserts IBAN is on one line or moved as block.
billing-bot: Invoice generator v2 — deploy log: 2026-03-16T08:12:04Z deployed to hosted-billing (build 2026.3.16.08).
Sergio (engineering): I'll open PR with template changes and include test artifacts. Adding @Olivia for legal wording review.
Olivia (legal): I'll do a wording pass and push accepted text. If we change header semantics, update invoice schema docs for customers.
Maria (billing): Thanks all. I'll keep the CS thread updated.
Noah (support): :thumbsup:
